behaviourPage.aStopStopsTheAgent: A stop stops the agent. A correction or an answer goes into what it is doing, or restarts it if its engine can't take words midway. Each agent can choose for itself in its own settings.
behaviourPage.agentsCanNameTheTask: Agents can name the task when they hand work on. With this set, a reviewer moving from one task to the next isn't stopped as if it were one long exchange. Calling the same work by another name doesn't get past the total, and your next message resets both counts.
behaviourPage.agentsStopAfterThisMany: Agents stop after this many replies to each other, so they can't use up your plan on their own. Your next message resets the count.
behaviourPage.alsoShowFilesThatChanged: Also show files that changed while an agent was working, not only its own.
behaviourPage.backgroundFootnote: For agents on Claude Code. While it waits, what you send goes into that turn or waits for it like any other, and a background task that makes no progress for the time under Stop stuck tool calls is stopped. Each agent can choose for itself in its own settings.
behaviourPage.between1And5In: Between 1 and 5 in the morning, while an agent is idle: notes marked (until a date) go after that date, repeats are merged, and anything contradicted moves to an archive with why. Each night's changes are in that agent's Memory page, with Undo, and the morning brief mentions them.
behaviourPage.bloksSearchesTheAgentsOthe: Bloks searches the agent's other chats and notes for close matches to your message. Up to three short notes go with that message only, each saying where it came from, and your message shows what was added. Rooms and email from people you haven't listed never get them.
behaviourPage.budget.each_one: Each task agents name gets {count} reply in a row, and all of them together stop at {total}.
behaviourPage.budget.each_other: Each task agents name gets {count} replies in a row, and all of them together stop at {total}.
behaviourPage.budget.noHigher: No higher than the limit above, so that limit still counts every reply in a row.
behaviourPage.budget.off: Off. The limit above counts every reply in a row, whatever the task.
behaviourPage.claudeCodeCodexAndPi: Claude Code, Codex and Pi re-send the whole chat with every tool call, so one reply in a long chat can use millions of tokens. Past this size, or 60% of the model's limit, the chat is compacted before your next message. The chat marks where.
behaviourPage.claudeCodeKeepsAChat: Claude Code keeps a chat cached for an hour. The first message after that re-sends the whole chat, which costs the most. With this on, a Claude Code chat over 100k tokens that has been quiet for 55 minutes is compacted while still cached. Some detail is lost, and the chat marks where.
behaviourPage.compactLongClaudeCodeChats: Compact long Claude Code chats before their cache expires.
behaviourPage.eachRoomChoosesWhoAnswers: Each room chooses who answers in its own menu: everyone, only the lead, or Auto.
behaviourPage.forClaudeCodeCodexAnd: For Claude Code, Codex and Pi. Compact before the next message once a chat reaches this size.
behaviourPage.handFailuresToALead: Hand failures to a lead, and show you what needs you.
behaviourPage.inARoomSetTo: In a room set to Auto, a message that names nobody goes first to a small model, which picks who answers from each agent's name, role and brief and the last few messages. It has 2.5 seconds; if it runs out, is unsure or can't be reached, the lead answers. Naming someone with @ never asks it.
behaviourPage.inARoomTheRooms: In a room, the room's lead goes first. Elsewhere, this.
behaviourPage.keepEachAgentsNotesShort: Keep each agent's notes short and current while you sleep.
behaviourPage.learn.moreSays: Also after shorter ones, and after any skill that was used for real work. At most {count} checks a day.
behaviourPage.learn.offSays: No checks, so nothing is spent.
behaviourPage.learn.suggestSays: After a chat that clearly worked something out, or a skill you corrected. At most {count} checks a day.
behaviourPage.longChatsGetSummarisedTo: Long chats get summarised to keep fitting. Off: all at once when full, with a short pause. On: a little after each reply, so no pause, but the provider can't reuse its cache, which costs more on some. Your own messages are never summarised.
behaviourPage.mostAgentRepliesInA: Most agent replies in a row
behaviourPage.mostAgentRepliesInARow: Most agent replies in a row across separate tasks
behaviourPage.nothingChangesOnItsOwn: Nothing changes on its own. New skills and changes to yours wait in Skills, with the reason, for you to keep, edit or dismiss. Each check is a call to the agent's own model, two when it changes a skill you have, on your plan or key.
behaviourPage.remindAnAgentWhatIt: Remind an agent what it said elsewhere that matches your message.
behaviourPage.router.allowance: One short call to {name} for each message that names nobody, from your Bloks AI allowance.
behaviourPage.router.claude: One short call to {model} for each message that names nobody, on your Claude plan. Each call starts Claude Code, which can take longer than Auto waits; then the lead answers.
behaviourPage.router.large: One short call to {model} for each message that names nobody, billed like any other use of {name}. Not a small model, so it costs more and may be slower.
behaviourPage.router.room: A small model from an engine the room's agents already use, so its messages go nowhere new. One short call for each message that names nobody.
behaviourPage.router.small: One short call to {model} for each message that names nobody, billed to your {name} key. A small model: usually a fraction of a cent.
behaviourPage.sometimesACommandWaitsOn: Sometimes a command waits on something that never answers. After this long with no progress, Bloks stops the reply and tells you and the agent which call it was. Thinking, writing and commands that keep reporting are never cut short. Time waiting on your approval doesn't count.
behaviourPage.stopWhenOneCallMakes: Stop when one call makes no progress for this long.
behaviourPage.summariseALittleAfterEach: Summarise a little after each reply, not all at once.
behaviourPage.thatEngineIsNoLonger: That engine is no longer here, so Auto rooms are on their lead. Choose another.
behaviourPage.whenAReplyFailsA: When a reply fails, a tool call gets stuck, or a routine, watcher or workflow fails, whoever leads gets a quiet turn to deal with it: try it once more, pass it to a teammate, or ask you. Nothing is tried again more than once, and if many things fail in an hour you get one summary instead of a card each.

starters.anyRole.1.label: What can you do?
starters.anyRole.1.prompt: What are the three most useful things you could take off my plate this week? Keep it short.
starters.anyRole.2.label: Get to know me
starters.anyRole.2.prompt: Ask me five quick questions so you understand how I work and what matters to me.
starters.anyRole.3.label: Start on a task
starters.anyRole.3.prompt: Here is what I need help with today:
starters.bookkeeper.1.label: Code my expenses
starters.bookkeeper.1.prompt: Categorize my recent transactions, and ask me about anything unclear instead of guessing.
starters.bookkeeper.2.label: Find missing receipts
starters.bookkeeper.2.prompt: Find the charges with no receipt, and list the ones only I can track down.
starters.bookkeeper.3.label: Close the month
starters.bookkeeper.3.prompt: Reconcile last month and tell me where the money actually went.
starters.chiefOfStaff.1.label: Brief me on today
starters.chiefOfStaff.1.prompt: Pull together what needs my attention today, and lead with the decisions only I can make.
starters.chiefOfStaff.2.label: Review my week
starters.chiefOfStaff.2.prompt: Review my week so far: what moved, what slipped, and the biggest risk to next week.
starters.chiefOfStaff.3.label: Prep a meeting
starters.chiefOfStaff.3.prompt: Help me prepare for my next meeting. Ask me who it is with and what it is about, then draft an agenda.
starters.engineer.1.label: Explain this codebase
starters.engineer.1.prompt: Give me a short tour of this codebase: what it does, how it is laid out, and where to start reading.
starters.engineer.2.label: Review my changes
starters.engineer.2.prompt: Review the uncommitted changes in this folder for correctness bugs, most severe first.
starters.engineer.3.label: Fix a bug
starters.engineer.3.prompt: Reproduce this bug, find the root cause, and tell me the fix before you change anything:
starters.growthMarketer.1.label: Plan a campaign
starters.growthMarketer.1.prompt: Help me plan a campaign. Ask me the goal, then give me the audience, message, channels and one success metric.
starters.growthMarketer.2.label: Write copy angles
starters.growthMarketer.2.prompt: Write three angles for this, each with the hypothesis it tests:
starters.growthMarketer.3.label: Audit a landing page
starters.growthMarketer.3.prompt: Review this landing page for clarity, proof, and one obvious next step:
starters.inboxManager.1.label: Triage my inbox
starters.inboxManager.1.prompt: Sort my unread email into needs me, routine, and noise. Explain any judgment call in one line.
starters.inboxManager.2.label: Draft routine replies
starters.inboxManager.2.prompt: Draft replies to the routine email waiting on me, in my voice, and hold them for my approval.
starters.inboxManager.3.label: Find what is urgent
starters.inboxManager.3.prompt: Find anything in my inbox that is time sensitive, financial or legal, and bring it to me first.
starters.ops.1.label: Run a health check
starters.ops.1.prompt: Check the tools and systems I depend on, and tell me what is broken or drifting.
starters.ops.2.label: Clean up records
starters.ops.2.prompt: Find duplicates, stale records and missing fields in my data, and propose a cleanup before changing anything.
starters.ops.3.label: Find a routine
starters.ops.3.prompt: Look at what I keep doing by hand, and suggest one task worth turning into a routine.
starters.personalAssistant.1.label: Book something
starters.personalAssistant.1.prompt: Help me book something. Ask me what, when and my budget, then hold the best option for my approval.
starters.personalAssistant.2.label: Track my renewals
starters.personalAssistant.2.prompt: List my subscriptions, licences and documents with their renewal dates, and remind me before each one lapses.
starters.personalAssistant.3.label: Clear my errands
starters.personalAssistant.3.prompt: Here are the small things on my plate. Take what you can and tell me what needs me:
starters.recruiter.1.label: Write a role brief
starters.recruiter.1.prompt: Turn this hiring need into a scorecard with must haves, nice to haves, and the bar:

starters.recruiter.2.prompt: Review these applicants for signal over pedigree and flag the ones worth my time.
starters.recruiter.3.label: Reach out to someone
starters.recruiter.3.prompt: Write a short, human note to this candidate that mentions their actual work:
starters.researchAnalyst.1.label: Research a topic
starters.researchAnalyst.1.prompt: Research this and give me a one page brief with sources:
starters.researchAnalyst.2.label: Map the competition
starters.researchAnalyst.2.prompt: Map the main players in my space: what they ship, how they price, and how they position. Ask me which space first.
starters.researchAnalyst.3.label: Check a claim
starters.researchAnalyst.3.prompt: Check this claim and tell me what the evidence actually supports:
starters.salesOutbound.1.label: Research a prospect
starters.salesOutbound.1.prompt: Research this company: what they do, what changed recently, and the best way in:
starters.salesOutbound.2.label: Draft outreach
starters.salesOutbound.2.prompt: Draft a short outreach email in my voice that mentions something specific about:
starters.salesOutbound.3.label: Chase the quiet ones
starters.salesOutbound.3.prompt: List the prospects who have gone quiet and draft the next follow up for each.
